page: Amazon Web Services h1.2xlarge is an instance in the storage-optimized family running on the Xen hypervisor. The virtual machine provides 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores and 8 threads, backed by a dedicated Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor operating at 2.3 GHz. Memory capacity totals 32.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a 4.0 GB per physical core density. Hardware acceleration via GPUs is not present. Storage is provisioned locally with a bundled 2000 GB hard disk drive (HDD), accompanied by a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile.

Benchmark results demonstrate modest computing and throughput performance characteristic of older Intel Broadwell-era silicon. The CPU scored 883.18 on single-core stress-ng tests and 904.0 in Geekbench single-core evaluations, placing compute responsiveness in the bottom decile. Multi-threaded evaluations similarly placed in the bottom quartile, with a stress-ng multi-core result of 4177.44 and Geekbench multi-core at 3371.0. Memory throughput delivered uncached read speeds of 38.02 GB/s and write speeds of 22.65 GB/s. High-throughput data processing operations showed lower capacity, with Redis throughput recording 2.51 million SET operations per second and static web throughput achieving 5.36 GB/s.

From an architectural efficiency perspective, the h1.2xlarge trades per-core compute capability and solid-state IOPS for dense, low-cost magnetic disk storage. Workloads needing rapid transactional response or low-latency I/O will find the mechanical disk subsystem and legacy CPU architecture restrictive. However, applications oriented toward high-capacity sequential storage, batch processing, data archiving, log processing, and distributed batch file ingestion benefit from the local disk allocation coupled with dedicated computing threads.

The configuration allocates 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores, 32.0 GB of system memory, and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps without GPU hardware. Local storage is provided through a bundled 2000 GB HDD, emphasizing bulk capacity over high IOPS. Benchmark figures place its single-core and multi-core computational throughput within lower percentiles, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 3371.0 and Redis throughput of 2.51 million operations per second. Memory performance remains average, achieving 38.02 GB/s uncached read bandwidth. Given its balance of spinning storage capacity and dedicated execution threads, h1.2xlarge is oriented toward sequential data processing, log retention, ETL batch tasks, and legacy distributed file storage.
